key_cases.case_name: Dept. of Human Services v. G. D. W.
key_cases.holding: The court held that a child who is the subject of a dependency petition is not automatically a "party-opponent" of the state, so the child's out-of-court abuse statements were inadmissible as nonhearsay under OEC 801(4)(b)(A) absent evidence the child had taken an adverse position, and it reversed the jurisdictional and aggravated-circumstances judgments because the error was not harmless.
key_cases.relevance: Holds that an order terminating DHS custody and dismissing juvenile court jurisdiction does not moot a parent's challenge to the underlying jurisdictional judgment.
key_cases.quote: We agree with father that the juvenile court erred in admitting the child's statements under OEC 801(4)(b)(A), and we conclude that the error was not harmless.

key_cases.case_name: Dept. of Human Services v. A. B.
key_cases.holding: The court held that when wardship is terminated during an appeal, the department — not the parent — bears the burden of proving the jurisdictional judgment will have no practical effect, and here it carried that burden.
key_cases.relevance: Governs the mootness consequences of dismissal or termination of wardship for a pending appeal.
key_cases.quote: The burden is on the department to prove that a jurisdictional judgment will have no practical effect on the rights of the parties and is therefore moot.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that it generally may review a constitutional ruling at the behest of a government official who prevailed below on qualified immunity, but that this Oregon case had become moot because the child had grown up and moved away, and it therefore vacated the part of the Ninth Circuit's opinion deciding the Fourth Amendment question about the in-school interview.
key_cases.relevance: Shows when a dependency-related federal appeal becomes moot because the child has outgrown the challenged practice, and what happens to the ruling below when it does.
key_cases.quote: we vacate the part of the Ninth Circuit's opinion that decided the Fourth Amendment issue.

key_cases.case_name: Dept. of Human Services v. T. J. N.
key_cases.holding: The court held the Court of Appeals erred in dismissing the parents' placement appeals as moot because the moving party had not persuaded the court that dismissal was warranted, though the appeals had since become moot for other reasons.
key_cases.relevance: Governs when a dependency appeal survives intervening dismissal or supersession of the underlying judgment, and places the persuasion burden on the party seeking dismissal.
key_cases.quote: But unless the moving party "persuades the appellate court that the dismissal is warranted," the appeal is not moot.
